verdict: Starbucks grew revenue 5% to $9.6B and global comparable sales rose 1% — the first increase in seven quarters — but $755M of restructuring charges for closing 627 stores cut net earnings 85% to $133M.

kpis.label: Global comparable sales
kpis.note: first growth in seven quarters; transactions +1%

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: -85% YoY on restructuring charges; non-GAAP EPS was $0.52

segments.name: North America
segments.note: Coffeehouses in the U.S. and Canada — comparable store sales were flat, with a 1% higher average ticket offsetting 1% fewer transactions.

segments.name: International
segments.note: Coffeehouses outside North America — comparable sales rose 3%, with China comps up 2% on 9% more transactions.

segments.name: Channel Development
segments.note: Packaged coffee and ready-to-drink drinks sold in grocery and convenience stores — growth came from the Global Coffee Alliance.

segments.name: Corporate & other
segments.note: Small leftover businesses and unallocated items.

opex.note: Running the company — roughly flat YoY.

opex.note: Wear and tear on coffeehouses, roasteries and equipment.

opex.name: Restructuring & impairments
opex.note: Closing 627 coffeehouses — over 90% of them in North America — and simplifying the support organization under 'Back to Starbucks'; the year-ago quarter had none.

follow100Note: Starbucks reports in tenths of a million; the figures on this page are rounded to whole $M.

takeaways.title: Comp growth is back
takeaways.text: Global comparable store sales rose 1% — the first growth in seven quarters — on 1% more transactions. U.S. comps were flat (ticket +1%, transactions -1%) and turned positive in September; International comps rose 3% and China's 2%.

takeaways.title: The bill for closing 627 stores
takeaways.text: Restructuring and impairment charges were $755M as Starbucks closed 627 coffeehouses under the plan announced September 25, 2025 — over 90% in North America — and simplified its support organization. The GAAP operating margin shrank to 2.9%; excluding such items it was 9.4%.

takeaways.title: The underlying quarter was steadier
takeaways.text: GAAP EPS was $0.12, down 85%. Excluding the restructuring charges and other one-offs, non-GAAP EPS was $0.52 — down 35%, but a fairer read on a business whose revenue grew 5%, ending the quarter with 40,990 stores after 107 net closures.

oneTimers: Restructuring and impairment charges were $755M under 'Back to Starbucks' — closing 627 coffeehouses (584 of them in North America) and simplifying the support organization; the year-ago quarter had none.
otherDetail: $85M of income from equity investees and $32M of interest and other income, less $146M of interest expense.
footerNote: Reported operating income of $278M includes $85M of income from equity investees, shown here in Other income.
